sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
Scaler is one of India's best-known technology education companies. Founded by Abhimanyu Saxena and Anshuman Singh, it grew out of InterviewBit, the coding interview practice platform they launched in the mid-2010s, and expanded into Scaler Academy for working software engineers, data science and AI programs, the free learning library Scaler Topics, and two residential schools: Scaler School of Technology (SST) for undergraduate computer science and, more recently, AI and Business, and Scaler School of Business. Headquartered in Bengaluru, Scaler reported revenue of about ₹363 crore in FY25 and cut its losses by roughly 98% to near break-even.

In 2026, Scaler repositioned itself as an AI-native technology career platform, rebuilding its flagship program as Modern Software & AI Engineering and launching new programs such as a PGP in Business and AI. For PM candidates, that makes Scaler an interesting place: products span free content, practice platforms, expensive cohort-based programs, AI learning tools and physical campuses, and every product is judged by one hard question: did learners actually get better careers?

This guide covers the PM roles Scaler hires for, what interviewers look for, how the process typically works, compensation, and how to prepare.

> Why Scaler is a distinctive PM environment
> Ed-tech PMs balance learning outcomes, learner experience and sales efficiency. At Scaler, you will also work closely with instructors, mentors and admissions teams, so cross-functional judgment matters as much as product sense.

sections.heading: PM Role
sections.content:
Product managers at Scaler typically own one of these areas:

1. **Learning experience:** The platform learners use every day: live classes, recordings, assignments, contests, doubt resolution and progress tracking.
2. **AI learning products:** AI tutors, AI mock interviewers, personalised learning paths and evaluation tools.
3. **Free platforms and growth:** InterviewBit, Scaler Topics, masterclasses and the funnel from free learners to paid programs.
4. **Admissions and sales tools:** Lead management, counselling workflows, entrance tests and payment and financing flows.
5. **Careers:** Job boards, employer partnerships, resume tools and outcome tracking.
6. **Campus products:** Systems for Scaler School of Technology and Scaler School of Business students, faculty and parents.

**Day-to-day responsibilities:**

- Analyse learner funnels and engagement, and design experiments.
- Work with instructors and curriculum teams to turn learning goals into product features.
- Partner with admissions and marketing on conversion and lead quality.
- Write specifications and prioritise backlogs with engineering and design.
- Track outcome metrics such as completion, interview readiness and placements.

Candidates report that the role titles include Associate Product Manager, Product Manager, Product Manager II and Senior Product Manager, with product intern roles for students.

> Expert Advice
> Show you understand that ed-tech success is measured by learner outcomes, not just engagement. Interviewers respond well to candidates who question vanity metrics.

sections.heading: Job Requirements
sections.content:
**For product interns and APMs:**

- Strong academic background, often engineering; coding familiarity is a plus because users are developers.
- Analytical skills: SQL, spreadsheets, funnel analysis.
- Structured problem solving and clear writing.
- Genuine interest in education and learning.

**For PM and PM II roles:**

- 2–6 years of product or related experience, ideally in consumer apps, ed-tech, SaaS or marketplaces.
- Experience with experimentation and growth funnels.
- Ability to work with non-product stakeholders such as instructors and sales teams.

**For Senior PM roles:**

- 6+ years of experience owning a product area end to end.
- Track record of measurable outcomes and leading cross-functional teams.

| Skill | Why it matters at Scaler | How to show it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Learning outcome thinking | Programs are judged by careers | Tie features to completion and outcomes |
| Funnel and growth analysis | Free-to-paid conversion drives revenue | Break down conversion steps |
| Empathy for developers | Learners are engineers and aspiring engineers | Use developer pain points in examples |
| AI product sense | Scaler is AI-native | Discuss evaluation, cost and failure modes of AI tutors |
| Stakeholder management | Instructors, mentors, sales | Show how you aligned different teams |

sections.heading: Interview Process Breakdown
sections.content:
Public reports on Scaler's PM interviews are limited, so treat this as a typical pattern. One Glassdoor review for a Product Manager II role in Bengaluru described a process of around three weeks that included an assignment.

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Recruiter Screen]
    B --> C[Assignment]
    C --> D[Product Case Interview]
    D --> E[Hiring Manager Round]
    E --> F[Founder or Leadership Round]
    F --> G[Offer]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus Areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recruiter screen | Phone or video | 20–30 mins | Background, motivation, why Scaler |
| Assignment | Take-home | 2–4 days | Product problem on a Scaler product, often with data |
| Product case interview | Video | 45–60 mins | Discussion of assignment, product design or metrics case |
| Hiring manager round | Video | 45 mins | Past projects, execution, collaboration |
| Leadership round | Video or in person | 30–45 mins | Strategy, ownership, culture fit |

**Detailed Breakdown:**

- Recruiter Screen:

Expect questions about your interest in education and what you know about Scaler's products. Candidates in other roles report being asked what they know about Scaler, so research before the call.

- Assignment:

A take-home problem, such as improving retention on InterviewBit or measuring a program feature. Interviewers typically look for clear problem framing, data-informed prioritisation and realistic metrics.

- Product Case Interview:

A deep discussion of your assignment, plus a live case. Common themes: learner engagement, funnel conversion, AI tutor design and outcome metrics.

- Hiring Manager Round:

Focused on your past work and how you collaborate with engineers, designers and non-product teams.

- Leadership Round:

May involve senior leaders. Expect questions on Scaler's strategy, the future of tech careers in the AI era, and your long-term goals.

Timeline expectations:

- About two to four weeks from first call to offer.
- Assignments usually come with a short deadline, so plan time accordingly.

sections.heading: Product Manager Compensation & Levels at Scaler
sections.content:
Scaler's compensation is typically a fixed salary plus performance bonus, with ESOPs for some roles given its startup structure (backed by investors such as Peak XV, Tiger Global and Lightrock).

| Level | Typical experience | Total annual compensation (INR, 2026 estimate) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product Intern | Students | Monthly stipend; annualised figures on AmbitionBox around ₹14–18 lakh |
| Associate Product Manager | 0–2 years | ₹12–20 lakh |
| Product Manager | 2–5 years | ₹20–34 lakh |
| Product Manager II or Senior PM | 5–8 years | ₹32–52 lakh |
| Lead or Group PM | 8–12 years | ₹48–75 lakh |
| Head of Product | 12+ years | ₹70 lakh–1.1 crore |

These figures are estimates based on limited self-reported data and comparable Bengaluru start-ups. See the salary guide for details.

sections.heading: How to Prepare
sections.content:
**Know the products:**

1. Solve problems on InterviewBit and read Scaler Topics articles.
2. Attend a free Scaler masterclass and note the funnel: registration, reminders, session, counselling call invitation.
3. Read about Scaler School of Technology and the 2026 program relaunches.
4. Follow founders' posts on LinkedIn for strategic signals.

**Practise ed-tech cases:**

- Design: an AI mock interviewer, a parent experience for SST.
- Improvement: InterviewBit retention, mentorship sessions.
- Metrics: Scaler Topics, the Modern Software & AI Engineering program.
- Root cause: masterclass conversion drops, assignment completion drops.
- Strategy and trade-offs: AI's impact on tech careers, live versus recorded classes, pricing models.

**Tailor your CV:** Highlight learner or user outcomes, experiments and cross-functional work. If you have taught, mentored or built learning tools, include it.

Use NextSprints' Resume Review service for detailed feedback, and practise with NextSprints' Product Manager Interview Questions.

- Strong academic background, often engineering; coding familiarity is a plus because users are developers.
- Analytical skills: SQL, spreadsheets, funnel analysis.
- Structured problem solving and clear writing.

**For PM and PM II roles:**

- 2–6 years of product or related experience, ideally in consumer apps, ed-tech, SaaS or marketplaces.
- Experience with experimentation and growth funnels.
- Ability to work with non-product stakeholders such as instructors and sales teams.

```mermaid
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Recruiter Screen]
    B --> C[Assignment]
    C --> D[Product Case Interview]
    D --> E[Hiring Manager Round]
    E --> F[Founder or Leadership Round]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus Areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recruiter screen | Phone or video | 20–30 mins | Background, motivation, why Scaler |
| Assignment | Take-home | 2–4 days | Product problem on a Scaler product, often with data |
| Product case interview | Video | 45–60 mins | Discussion of assignment, product design or metrics case |

- Product Case Interview:

A deep discussion of your assignment, plus a live case. Common themes: learner engagement, funnel conversion, AI tutor design and outcome metrics.

- Hiring Manager Round:

Focused on your past work and how you collaborate with engineers, designers and non-product teams.

- Leadership Round:

May involve senior leaders. Expect questions on Scaler's strategy, the future of tech careers in the AI era, and your long-term goals.

Candidates have reported an assignment as part of the PM process. Expect a problem tied to a Scaler product, followed by a discussion where interviewers probe your assumptions and metrics.

Because Scaler's users are engineers and aspiring engineers, being comfortable with coding concepts helps you empathise with learners and work with engineering teams. You are not expected to code in interviews, but you should understand the learning journey of a developer.

Scaler has rebuilt its flagship programs around AI, launched AI-focused programs and positioned itself as AI-native. PM candidates should be ready to discuss how AI changes both what Scaler teaches and how it teaches.

State Bank of India is not the first name most students think of when they hear "product manager". Yet SBI runs some of the largest digital products in India. YONO has more than 10 crore registered users, YONO 2.0 launched in December 2025 with a goal of reaching 20 crore users in two years, and around two-thirds of new SBI savings accounts are now opened digitally. Around YONO sit YONO Business for corporates and MSMEs, BHIM SBI Pay for UPI, and group companies such as SBI Card, SBI Life, SBI Mutual Fund and SBICAP Securities, each with its own digital teams.

sections.content:
SBI's process for regular specialist officer posts is more formal than a private company's, and decisions rest heavily on one interview.

```mermaid
graph LR
```

sections.content:

sections.heading: How to Prepare
sections.content:
1. **Know SBI's digital products.** Use YONO 2.0, YONO Business (if you can), BHIM SBI Pay and the SBI Card app. Note what works and what frustrates users.
2. **Learn the basics of Indian digital banking.** UPI, IMPS, NEFT, RTGS, video KYC, Account Aggregator, credit on UPI, and RBI rules on digital lending.
3. **Read recent news.** YONO 2.0 launch and migration, the 20 crore user goal, the July 2026 Bank Day launches (Financial Fitness, 3-in-1 account, YONO Business trade finance, YONO Ji), and SBI Card's digital partnerships such as Google Pay Flex.
4. **Prepare product stories.** Two or three examples where you owned a product, used data to make decisions and handled stakeholders, ideally in a regulated setting.
5. **Practise product cases with an Indian lens.** For example: how would you get rural customers onto YONO, or why did digital account openings drop?

> Practice questions
> Work through the State Bank of India questions on NextSprints, such as measuring YONO 2.0's success, designing YONO for first-time digital users, or diagnosing a drop in YONO's pre-approved loan disbursals.

subsections.heading: Does SBI hire freshers into product roles?
subsections.content: Regular product roles under SCO recruitment usually require prior experience, typically two or more years for Deputy Manager. Freshers can join SBI as Probationary Officers through the PO exam and later move into digital teams, or join SBI group companies such as SBI Card, which hire some MBA graduates into product and digital roles.

subsections.heading: What kind of questions are asked in the SBI product interview?
subsections.content: Candidates report a mix of questions about their own experience, digital banking concepts and SBI's products. Expect questions such as "How would you improve YONO?", "How do you prevent UPI fraud?", "Explain video KYC" and "Describe a product you launched and its results." Some panels ask about general banking and current affairs.

subsections.heading: How technical do SBI product managers need to be?
subsections.content: Many product posts require an engineering or MCA degree. You should understand APIs, system integration, mobile app performance and security basics, because much of the work involves coordinating vendors and IT teams. You do not need to code in the interview.

subsections.heading: Is the selection only one interview?
subsections.content: For regular SCO posts, recent notifications describe shortlisting followed by an interview, with merit based on interview marks. Some posts in the past included written tests. Contract posts add CTC negotiation. Always read the specific notification.

subsections.heading: Where are SBI's digital product roles based?
subsections.content: Most are in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, at SBI's Corporate Centre and Global IT Centre. Some roles may be in other cities depending on the department. Group companies are mostly in Mumbai and Gurugram (SBI Card).

subsections.heading: How is working as a PM at SBI different from a fintech?
subsections.content: The scale and impact are much larger, but decisions take longer and pass through more approvals. PMs work more with vendors and governance processes. In return, they get stability, strong benefits, and the chance to shape banking for a huge share of India.

Candidates report a mix of questions about their own experience, digital banking concepts and SBI's products. Expect questions such as "How would you improve YONO?", "How do you prevent UPI fraud?", "Explain video KYC" and "Describe a product you launched and its results." Some panels ask about general banking and current affairs.

### How technical do SBI product managers need to be?

Many product posts require an engineering or MCA degree. You should understand APIs, system integration, mobile app performance and security basics, because much of the work involves coordinating vendors and IT teams. You do not need to code in the interview.

### Is the selection only one interview?

For regular SCO posts, recent notifications describe shortlisting followed by an interview, with merit based on interview marks. Some posts in the past included written tests. Contract posts add CTC negotiation. Always read the specific notification.

### Where are SBI's digital product roles based?

Most are in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai, at SBI's Corporate Centre and Global IT Centre. Some roles may be in other cities depending on the department. Group companies are mostly in Mumbai and Gurugram (SBI Card).

### How is working as a PM at SBI different from a fintech?

The scale and impact are much larger, but decisions take longer and pass through more approvals. PMs work more with vendors and governance processes. In return, they get stability, strong benefits, and the chance to shape banking for a huge share of India.

title: Tata Digital Product Manager Interview Guide | Tata Neu

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
Tata Digital is the Tata Group's consumer technology arm and the company behind Tata Neu, the group's super app launched in April 2022. Its portfolio covers BigBasket (groceries and BB Now quick commerce), Tata 1mg (pharmacy and diagnostics), Croma (electronics), Tata CLiQ (fashion and lifestyle), Tata Pay UPI, Neu Finance (personal loans, insurance and investments through partners), and the NeuCoins and NeuPass loyalty program used across Tata brands such as Air India, IHCL, Westside and Titan. The Tata Neu HDFC Bank and Tata Neu SBI co-branded credit cards sit on top of that loyalty layer.

Product management at Tata Digital is shaped by a clear strategic reset. In FY26, the digital group reported revenue of about ₹35,990 crore and a net loss of about ₹4,974 crore, with BigBasket the largest drag. Since CEO Sajith Sivanandan took charge in September 2025, Tata Digital has moved away from GMV-led growth toward loyalty, financial services and monetisation across the group. For PM candidates, this means interviews lean heavily on unit economics, loyalty design, payments and credit, and making trade-offs between growth and profitability.

| Hiring Metric | Value (estimated) |
| --- | --- |
| Typical PM interview rounds | 3–5 (AmbitionBox reports 2–3 for many roles) |
| Reported interview difficulty | About 3 out of 5 (Glassdoor) |
| Typical time from first call to offer | 2–4 weeks for lateral hires |
| Main PM locations | Bengaluru and Mumbai (1mg teams in Gurugram) |
| Campus PM intake | Small; mostly via MBA internships converting to PPOs |

> What Candidates Report
> Candidates report that interviewers care less about textbook frameworks and more about whether you understand how money flows in the ecosystem: who funds a NeuCoin, what a UPI payment earns, and why BigBasket's dark-store density matters.

sections.heading: PM Role
sections.content:
> Tata Digital Product Manager
> A Tata Digital Product Manager owns a part of the Tata Neu ecosystem (such as loyalty, payments, lending, a brand integration or a commerce vertical) and balances customer experience, partner economics (banks, lenders, Tata brands) and regulatory constraints to grow engagement and profitable revenue.

Responsibilities:

- Define roadmaps for areas such as NeuCoins and NeuPass, Tata Pay UPI, Neu Finance, or the Tata Neu home and checkout
- Work with Tata brand teams (BigBasket, Croma, 1mg, CLiQ) on shared loyalty and identity
- Partner with banks and lenders (HDFC Bank, SBI Card, Tata Capital and others) on card, credit and insurance journeys
- Write PRDs, define metrics, and run experiments with engineering, design and analytics
- Model unit economics: reward cost, interchange, distribution fees, contribution margin
- Ensure compliance with RBI, NPCI and consumer-protection rules in collaboration with legal and risk teams

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[CEO, Tata Digital] --> B[Head of Product / CPTO]
    B --> C[Loyalty Platform: NeuCoins, NeuPass]
    B --> D[Payments: Tata Pay UPI, Cards]
    B --> E[Neu Finance: Loans, Insurance]
    B --> F[Tata Neu App and Brand Integrations]
    C --> G[PM - Earn and Burn Engine]
    D --> H[PM - UPI and Credit on UPI]
    E --> I[PM - Lending Marketplace]
    F --> J[PM - Home, Search and Checkout]
```

The chart is illustrative; portfolio companies such as BigBasket and Tata 1mg run their own product organisations with separate hiring.

| Aspect | Tata Digital PM | Consumer Startup PM | Big Tech PM in India |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Focus | Ecosystem, loyalty, fintech | Single product growth | Platform scale |
| Pace | Fast, with group governance | Very fast | Fast |
| Partner management | Very high (banks, brands) | Moderate | Moderate |
| Regulatory involvement | High in finance and payments | Varies | Moderate |
| Business acumen expected | Very high (P&L pressure) | High | Moderate |

Real-world example: when Tata Neu introduced 12-month validity for NeuCoins from August 2025 and tightened some UPI earn rules on co-branded cards, PMs had to balance loyalty cost against user trust, coordinate with bank partners, and redesign expiry communication in the app.

sections.heading: Job Requirements
sections.content:
Common titles: Associate Product Manager, Product Manager, Senior Product Manager, Lead/Principal Product Manager, and Director of Product. Some roles are posted as Product Owner or Product Lead.

Typical requirements by level:

- APM / campus hire: MBA from a top B-school (IIMs, ISB, FMS, XLRI, SPJIMR) or engineering degree from IITs/NITs with a strong internship; 0–2 years of experience
- PM: 2–5 years in product, ideally in consumer internet, e-commerce, payments or fintech
- Senior PM: 5–8 years with ownership of a live product and measurable outcomes
- Lead PM and above: 8+ years, team leadership, partner negotiation experience

Skills interviewers look for:

- Product sense for Indian consumers across metros and Tier-2 cities
- Analytical ability: SQL, funnel analysis, cohort retention, A/B testing
- Business and unit economics, especially for loyalty, quick commerce and lending
- Understanding of UPI, credit cards, RBI digital lending rules and NPCI frameworks for fintech roles
- Stakeholder management across Tata brands and external partners
- Clear written communication (PRDs, one-pagers)

> Expert Advice
> Quantify impact in your resume with business outcomes (conversion, retention, cost per order) rather than features shipped. Tata Digital interviewers often ask how a feature affected the P&L.

```mermaid
graph LR

    D --> E[Analytics or Assignment]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus Areas |

| Recruiter Screen | Phone | 20–30 mins | Background, motivation, notice period, expectations |
| Hiring Manager | Video | 45–60 mins | Past products, depth of ownership, domain fit |

| Analytics / Assignment | Video or take-home | 45 mins or 2–3 days | Metrics, RCA, SQL-style reasoning, or a written PRD |
| Leadership + HR | In person or video | 30–45 mins each | Strategy, culture fit, compensation |

Detailed Breakdown:

- Recruiter Screen:

Basic fit check covering your experience, why Tata Digital, and compensation expectations. Expect questions on why you want to work in a conglomerate-backed company versus a startup.

- Product Case Round:

Typical prompts include designing a feature for NeuPass, improving Tata 1mg's refill journey, or making Croma's online-to-store experience better. Interviewers expect clear segmentation, prioritisation and metrics.

- Analytics or Assignment:

Root cause analysis (for example, a drop in BB Now repeat orders) or a metrics question (how to measure NeuCoins' success). Some teams give a take-home case with a short presentation.

content_markdown:
## Introduction

Tata Digital is the Tata Group's consumer technology arm and the company behind Tata Neu, the group's super app launched in April 2022. Its portfolio covers BigBasket (groceries and BB Now quick commerce), Tata 1mg (pharmacy and diagnostics), Croma (electronics), Tata CLiQ (fashion and lifestyle), Tata Pay UPI, Neu Finance (personal loans, insurance and investments through partners), and the NeuCoins and NeuPass loyalty program used across Tata brands such as Air India, IHCL, Westside and Titan. The Tata Neu HDFC Bank and Tata Neu SBI co-branded credit cards sit on top of that loyalty layer.

Product management at Tata Digital is shaped by a clear strategic reset. In FY26, the digital group reported revenue of about ₹35,990 crore and a net loss of about ₹4,974 crore, with BigBasket the largest drag. Since CEO Sajith Sivanandan took charge in September 2025, Tata Digital has moved away from GMV-led growth toward loyalty, financial services and monetisation across the group. For PM candidates, this means interviews lean heavily on unit economics, loyalty design, payments and credit, and making trade-offs between growth and profitability.

| Hiring Metric | Value (estimated) |
| --- | --- |
| Typical PM interview rounds | 3–5 (AmbitionBox reports 2–3 for many roles) |
| Reported interview difficulty | About 3 out of 5 (Glassdoor) |
| Typical time from first call to offer | 2–4 weeks for lateral hires |
| Main PM locations | Bengaluru and Mumbai (1mg teams in Gurugram) |
| Campus PM intake | Small; mostly via MBA internships converting to PPOs |

> What Candidates Report
> Candidates report that interviewers care less about textbook frameworks and more about whether you understand how money flows in the ecosystem: who funds a NeuCoin, what a UPI payment earns, and why BigBasket's dark-store density matters.

## PM Role

> Tata Digital Product Manager
> A Tata Digital Product Manager owns a part of the Tata Neu ecosystem (such as loyalty, payments, lending, a brand integration or a commerce vertical) and balances customer experience, partner economics (banks, lenders, Tata brands) and regulatory constraints to grow engagement and profitable revenue.

Responsibilities:

- Define roadmaps for areas such as NeuCoins and NeuPass, Tata Pay UPI, Neu Finance, or the Tata Neu home and checkout
- Work with Tata brand teams (BigBasket, Croma, 1mg, CLiQ) on shared loyalty and identity
- Partner with banks and lenders (HDFC Bank, SBI Card, Tata Capital and others) on card, credit and insurance journeys
- Write PRDs, define metrics, and run experiments with engineering, design and analytics
- Model unit economics: reward cost, interchange, distribution fees, contribution margin
- Ensure compliance with RBI, NPCI and consumer-protection rules in collaboration with legal and risk teams

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[CEO, Tata Digital] --> B[Head of Product / CPTO]
    B --> C[Loyalty Platform: NeuCoins, NeuPass]
    B --> D[Payments: Tata Pay UPI, Cards]
    B --> E[Neu Finance: Loans, Insurance]
    B --> F[Tata Neu App and Brand Integrations]
    C --> G[PM - Earn and Burn Engine]
    D --> H[PM - UPI and Credit on UPI]
    E --> I[PM - Lending Marketplace]
    F --> J[PM - Home, Search and Checkout]
```

The chart is illustrative; portfolio companies such as BigBasket and Tata 1mg run their own product organisations with separate hiring.

| Aspect | Tata Digital PM | Consumer Startup PM | Big Tech PM in India |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Focus | Ecosystem, loyalty, fintech | Single product growth | Platform scale |
| Pace | Fast, with group governance | Very fast | Fast |
| Partner management | Very high (banks, brands) | Moderate | Moderate |
| Regulatory involvement | High in finance and payments | Varies | Moderate |
| Business acumen expected | Very high (P&L pressure) | High | Moderate |

Real-world example: when Tata Neu introduced 12-month validity for NeuCoins from August 2025 and tightened some UPI earn rules on co-branded cards, PMs had to balance loyalty cost against user trust, coordinate with bank partners, and redesign expiry communication in the app.

## Job Requirements

Common titles: Associate Product Manager, Product Manager, Senior Product Manager, Lead/Principal Product Manager, and Director of Product. Some roles are posted as Product Owner or Product Lead.

Typical requirements by level:

- APM / campus hire: MBA from a top B-school (IIMs, ISB, FMS, XLRI, SPJIMR) or engineering degree from IITs/NITs with a strong internship; 0–2 years of experience
- PM: 2–5 years in product, ideally in consumer internet, e-commerce, payments or fintech
- Senior PM: 5–8 years with ownership of a live product and measurable outcomes
- Lead PM and above: 8+ years, team leadership, partner negotiation experience

Skills interviewers look for:

- Product sense for Indian consumers across metros and Tier-2 cities
- Analytical ability: SQL, funnel analysis, cohort retention, A/B testing
- Business and unit economics, especially for loyalty, quick commerce and lending
- Understanding of UPI, credit cards, RBI digital lending rules and NPCI frameworks for fintech roles
- Stakeholder management across Tata brands and external partners
- Clear written communication (PRDs, one-pagers)

> Expert Advice
> Quantify impact in your resume with business outcomes (conversion, retention, cost per order) rather than features shipped. Tata Digital interviewers often ask how a feature affected the P&L.

## Interview Process Breakdown

Lateral PM process as reported by candidates:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Recruiter Screen]
    B --> C[Hiring Manager Round]
    C --> D[Product Case Round]
    D --> E[Analytics or Assignment]
    E --> F[Leadership and HR]
    F --> G[Offer]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus Areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recruiter Screen | Phone | 20–30 mins | Background, motivation, notice period, expectations |
| Hiring Manager | Video | 45–60 mins | Past products, depth of ownership, domain fit |
| Product Case | Video or in person | 45–60 mins | Product design or improvement on a Tata Neu product |
| Analytics / Assignment | Video or take-home | 45 mins or 2–3 days | Metrics, RCA, SQL-style reasoning, or a written PRD |
| Leadership + HR | In person or video | 30–45 mins each | Strategy, culture fit, compensation |

Detailed Breakdown:

- Recruiter Screen:

Basic fit check covering your experience, why Tata Digital, and compensation expectations. Expect questions on why you want to work in a conglomerate-backed company versus a startup.

- Product Case Round:

Typical prompts include designing a feature for NeuPass, improving Tata 1mg's refill journey, or making Croma's online-to-store experience better. Interviewers expect clear segmentation, prioritisation and metrics.

- Analytics or Assignment:

Root cause analysis (for example, a drop in BB Now repeat orders) or a metrics question (how to measure NeuCoins' success). Some teams give a take-home case with a short presentation.

- Leadership Round:

Strategy questions about Tata Neu's direction, quick-commerce competition, or financial services. Candidates report questions such as "Should Tata Neu remain a super app?"

Campus process (MBA and engineering): pre-placement talk, CV shortlist, sometimes a case or group discussion, then two interview rounds on placement day covering a product case and a personal/HR discussion. Many campus PM hires come through summer internships converting to pre-placement offers.

Timeline Expectations:

- Lateral hires: 2–4 weeks from first call to offer
- Campus: decisions on the same day or within a week of interviews
- Feedback is usually shared through the recruiter within a few days

These ranges are anchored on AmbitionBox data (Product Manager ₹23–55 lakh for 2–9 years' experience; Senior PM ₹24.5–60.5 lakh in Mumbai) and extrapolated for other levels. Compensation is mainly fixed salary plus an annual performance bonus; equity-like long-term incentives are less common than at venture-backed startups. See our salary guide for detail.

## How to Prepare

Principles that matter at Tata Digital:

1. Trust first: the Tata brand carries high trust, especially in financial products. Show you won't trade it for short-term growth.
2. Ecosystem thinking: solutions should help more than one Tata brand.
3. Unit economics: know what a NeuCoin costs, what UPI earns, and why dark-store density matters.
4. Partner empathy: banks, lenders and Tata brands have their own goals.

Tailor Your Resume: Highlight measurable results, partner management, and any fintech, e-commerce or loyalty experience. Use the STAR method for achievements. For a review tailored to Tata Digital roles, consider NextSprints' Resume Review service.

Practice Product Cases:

- Loyalty design: NeuCoins, NeuPass, household rewards
- Payments: Tata Pay UPI, credit on UPI, reward economics
- Commerce: BigBasket quick commerce, Croma omnichannel, 1mg refills, CLiQ pricing
- Strategy: super app versus loyalty layer; competing with Reliance, Amazon and Flipkart

NextSprints' Product Manager Interview Questions include Tata Digital-specific cases on each of these.

Mock Interviews: Practise with PMs from Indian consumer internet or fintech companies who can push you on numbers. If you need one, NextSprints offers PM Coaching with experienced interviewers.

## FAQs

### Does Tata Digital have a formal APM program?

There is no widely publicised, branded APM program like those at some global tech companies. Candidates report that Tata Digital hires associate PMs through MBA campus placements and summer internships that convert to pre-placement offers, plus occasional off-campus hiring of engineers with 0–2 years of experience. Check placement reports from your institute and Tata Digital's careers page for current openings.

### How long does the Tata Digital PM interview process take?

For lateral hires, candidates typically report two to four weeks from the first recruiter call to an offer, with three to five rounds. AmbitionBox data for Tata Digital overall suggests many processes finish within about two weeks. Campus processes usually conclude on placement day or within a week.

### What kind of case questions are asked?

Expect product cases grounded in Tata's portfolio: improving NeuPass, measuring NeuCoins, diagnosing a drop in BigBasket orders, deciding on UPI reward rules, or planning Tata Neu's strategy. Interviewers value structured thinking, realistic Indian user personas and clear metrics.

### How technical do Tata Digital PM interviews get?

Most PM roles don't require coding, but you should be comfortable with APIs, data pipelines and basic SQL logic. Fintech roles expect familiarity with UPI flows, card networks, KYC, and RBI digital lending guidelines. Platform roles (loyalty engine, identity) may involve system design discussions at a high level.

### How should I talk about Tata Digital's losses in an interview?

Treat it as context, not criticism. Show you understand why the group is shifting toward loyalty and financial services, and how your work would improve unit economics. Interviewers appreciate candidates who can propose growth that pays for itself.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is India's largest IT services company, with roughly US$30 billion in annual revenue and around 6 lakh employees. Most students know TCS as a mass recruiter of engineers through the National Qualifier Test (NQT). Fewer know that TCS also runs a substantial products and platforms business, with software used by banks, insurers, retailers, governments and universities around the world. That is where most product manager and product owner roles sit.

Product roles at TCS fall into two broad groups. The first is the **Products and Platforms** units: TCS BaNCS (core banking, capital markets and insurance), ignio (AIOps from TCS subsidiary Digitate), TCS iON (assessments, exams and learning), TCS MasterCraft (including TransformPlus for legacy modernisation), TCS Optumera (AI retail merchandising) and TCS WisdomNext (GenAI orchestration, launched in 2024). The second is **client-facing digital product roles**, where TCS staff act as Product Owners on clients' agile programmes, for example owning a bank's mobile app backlog or a retailer's e-commerce journey.

In 2026, TCS is repositioning itself around AI. It reported AI services revenue of about US$2.3 billion annualised in FY26, launched a "Human+AI" operating model, and set up HyperVault, an AI data-centre subsidiary. For PM candidates, that means more product roles around AI platforms and AI features inside existing products.

| Hiring metric | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Product and product owner openings per year (India) | Several hundred, mostly lateral |
| Main campus entry routes | NQT (Ninja, Digital, Prime), MBA campus hiring |
| Typical rounds | 3–4 |
| Average time to offer (lateral) | 2–5 weeks |

> What makes TCS different
> Candidates report that TCS product interviews care less about consumer "product sense" puzzles and more about domain depth, stakeholder management and delivery discipline. A PM on TCS BaNCS who understands how a bank posts an interest accrual is more valuable than one who can design a fancy app screen.

sections.heading: PM Role
sections.content:
> TCS Product Manager
> A TCS Product Manager or Product Owner defines and delivers software products or product backlogs, either for TCS's own platforms (such as BaNCS, ignio or iON) or for clients' digital products, balancing customer needs, domain rules, delivery constraints and commercial goals.

Responsibilities:

- Own the roadmap and backlog for a product module (for example, BaNCS deposits or iON assessment engine)
- Translate client and market requirements into epics, user stories and acceptance criteria
- Work with architects, engineering, QA and implementation teams across India and onshore locations
- Support pre-sales: demos, RFP responses and solution walkthroughs for banks, retailers or governments
- Track adoption, defects and client satisfaction after releases
- Ensure compliance with domain regulations (banking, data protection, exam integrity)

Where PMs sit:

| Unit | Product focus | Typical PM work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TCS BaNCS | Core banking, payments, capital markets, insurance | Domain-heavy features, regulatory changes, cloud-native modules |
| ignio (Digitate) | AIOps, autonomous IT and business operations | Automation content, integrations, AI features |
| TCS iON | Exams, NQT, learning, campus software | High-scale B2G and B2C flows, candidate experience |
| TCS MasterCraft | TransformPlus, DataPlus, DevOps tools | Developer tools, GenAI-assisted modernisation |
| TCS Optumera | Retail merchandising AI | Forecasting, pricing, assortment UX |
| Client digital programmes | Banking apps, retail platforms, insurance portals | Product Owner on agile teams |

Locations: Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Gandhinagar and Delhi NCR, with onshore roles in the UK, US, Europe and the Middle East.

sections.heading: Job Requirements
sections.content:
Qualifications:

- Engineering, MBA or domain degrees (finance, commerce, retail) are common
- Lateral PM roles typically need 4–10 years of experience, often including business analysis or domain consulting
- Domain certifications help: banking (for example, IIBF courses), agile (CSPO, SAFe POPM), cloud fundamentals

Skills:

| Skill | Why it matters at TCS |
| --- | --- |
| Domain knowledge | BaNCS, Optumera and iON serve regulated, complex industries |
| Requirements and backlog management | Most work runs in agile or SAFe programmes |
| Stakeholder management | Clients, delivery leaders and onshore teams all have a say |
| Data and analytics | Adoption, defects and KPIs drive roadmap decisions |
| Communication | Pre-sales demos and client workshops are frequent |
| AI literacy | WisdomNext, ignio and AI features are now part of most roadmaps |

Experience level guide:

- **Campus (0–2 years):** Business analyst or associate product roles; learning the domain is expected
- **Product Owner / PM (4–9 years):** Owns a module or a client product backlog
- **Senior PM (8–13 years):** Owns a product line, influences pre-sales and roadmap
- **Product Head (12+ years):** Owns a product P&L and multiple teams

sections.heading: Interview Process Breakdown
sections.content:
Lateral process as reported by candidates on AmbitionBox, Glassdoor and Prepfully:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Online Assessment or Screening Call]
    B --> C[Technical and Product Round]
    C --> D[Managerial Round]
    D --> E[HR Round]
    E --> F[Offer]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Phone or iON-based test | 20–60 mins | Background, aptitude or domain basics |
| Technical and product | Video or in person | 45–60 mins | Product lifecycle, go-to-market, agile, domain case |
| Managerial | Video or in person | 30–60 mins | Stakeholder scenarios, client handling, prioritisation |
| HR | Phone or video | 20–30 mins | Compensation, notice period, relocation |

Detailed breakdown:

- Technical and product round:

Candidates report questions on the product lifecycle, writing user stories, defining MVPs and go-to-market plans. Domain teams add specifics: a BaNCS round may ask how a payment flows from UPI to the core ledger, while an iON round may ask how to scale an exam to lakhs of candidates.

- Managerial round:

Expect scenarios such as "A client wants a feature that conflicts with the product roadmap. What do you do?" or "Your release has a critical defect two days before go-live." Interviewers typically look for calm prioritisation and transparent communication.

- Product case:

Some teams ask a short case: design a feature, improve a metric or analyse a drop. Practising with TCS products (for example, improving NQT, measuring ignio success) gives you relevant examples.

- HR round:

Standard discussion of CTC, variable pay, location and joining date. TCS HR policies are structured, so negotiation room depends on level.

Campus process: graduates enter through TCS NQT and are assigned to Ninja, Digital or Prime tracks based on scores and interviews (technical, managerial, HR). MBA hiring at partner campuses includes a resume shortlist, sometimes a group discussion or case, and interviews for business analyst, domain consultant or product roles. Moving into product ownership usually happens after one to three years.

Timeline expectations:

- Lateral: 2–5 weeks
- Campus: results within days of interviews; joining dates can vary

sections.heading: How to Prepare
sections.content:
Preparation timeline:

1. **Weeks 1–2: Learn the domain.** Pick the unit you are targeting. For BaNCS, learn core banking basics: accounts, ledgers, interest, payments (UPI, NEFT, RTGS, SWIFT). For iON, learn how computer-based exams work. For ignio, read about AIOps and ITSM.
2. **Weeks 2–3: Practise product cases.** Design, improvement, metrics and RCA questions using TCS products.
3. **Week 3: Agile and delivery.** Be ready to write user stories, explain Scrum ceremonies and handle scope changes.
4. **Week 4: Behavioural stories.** Prepare stories on stakeholder conflict, delivery under pressure and influencing without authority.

Practice resources:

- TCS product pages and press releases (BaNCS, ignio, iON, WisdomNext)
- TCS annual reports and earnings call commentary for strategy context
- Gartner and analyst summaries on core banking and AIOps
- NextSprints TCS question bank

> Success tip
> Tie every answer back to client outcomes: fewer outages, faster product launches, lower costs or better exam reliability. TCS sells outcomes to enterprises and governments, and interviewers listen for that framing.

subsections.heading: Does TCS have a formal APM program?
subsections.content: TCS does not run a branded APM programme like some product companies. Graduates usually join through NQT or MBA campus hiring as engineers, business analysts or domain consultants, and move into product owner roles within one to three years. Units such as TCS iON, BaNCS and Digitate also hire associate-level product staff laterally.

subsections.heading: How technical are TCS product interviews?
subsections.content: Moderately technical. You are not expected to code, but you should understand APIs, integration, databases and cloud basics, especially for BaNCS and ignio roles. Candidates report questions on how systems interact and how they would handle defects or performance issues.

subsections.heading: Is domain knowledge mandatory?
subsections.content: For BaNCS and Optumera roles, strong domain knowledge is a major advantage and sometimes required. For iON and client digital programmes, general product skills plus a willingness to learn the domain can be enough at junior levels.

subsections.heading: How long does the TCS PM interview process take?
subsections.content: Lateral candidates typically report 2–5 weeks from first call to offer. Delays usually come from background verification and offer approvals rather than interviews.

subsections.heading: Can I move from a TCS engineering role into product management?
subsections.content: Yes. Internal mobility is common. Engineers often move to business analyst or product owner roles in client programmes, then into product units. Building domain expertise and taking ownership of requirements are the usual stepping stones.

content_markdown:
## Introduction

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is India's largest IT services company, with roughly US$30 billion in annual revenue and around 6 lakh employees. Most students know TCS as a mass recruiter of engineers through the National Qualifier Test (NQT). Fewer know that TCS also runs a substantial products and platforms business, with software used by banks, insurers, retailers, governments and universities around the world. That is where most product manager and product owner roles sit.

Product roles at TCS fall into two broad groups. The first is the **Products and Platforms** units: TCS BaNCS (core banking, capital markets and insurance), ignio (AIOps from TCS subsidiary Digitate), TCS iON (assessments, exams and learning), TCS MasterCraft (including TransformPlus for legacy modernisation), TCS Optumera (AI retail merchandising) and TCS WisdomNext (GenAI orchestration, launched in 2024). The second is **client-facing digital product roles**, where TCS staff act as Product Owners on clients' agile programmes, for example owning a bank's mobile app backlog or a retailer's e-commerce journey.

In 2026, TCS is repositioning itself around AI. It reported AI services revenue of about US$2.3 billion annualised in FY26, launched a "Human+AI" operating model, and set up HyperVault, an AI data-centre subsidiary. For PM candidates, that means more product roles around AI platforms and AI features inside existing products.

| Hiring metric | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Product and product owner openings per year (India) | Several hundred, mostly lateral |
| Main campus entry routes | NQT (Ninja, Digital, Prime), MBA campus hiring |
| Typical rounds | 3–4 |
| Average time to offer (lateral) | 2–5 weeks |

> What makes TCS different
> Candidates report that TCS product interviews care less about consumer "product sense" puzzles and more about domain depth, stakeholder management and delivery discipline. A PM on TCS BaNCS who understands how a bank posts an interest accrual is more valuable than one who can design a fancy app screen.

## PM Role

> TCS Product Manager
> A TCS Product Manager or Product Owner defines and delivers software products or product backlogs, either for TCS's own platforms (such as BaNCS, ignio or iON) or for clients' digital products, balancing customer needs, domain rules, delivery constraints and commercial goals.

Responsibilities:

- Own the roadmap and backlog for a product module (for example, BaNCS deposits or iON assessment engine)
- Translate client and market requirements into epics, user stories and acceptance criteria
- Work with architects, engineering, QA and implementation teams across India and onshore locations
- Support pre-sales: demos, RFP responses and solution walkthroughs for banks, retailers or governments
- Track adoption, defects and client satisfaction after releases
- Ensure compliance with domain regulations (banking, data protection, exam integrity)

Where PMs sit:

| Unit | Product focus | Typical PM work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TCS BaNCS | Core banking, payments, capital markets, insurance | Domain-heavy features, regulatory changes, cloud-native modules |
| ignio (Digitate) | AIOps, autonomous IT and business operations | Automation content, integrations, AI features |
| TCS iON | Exams, NQT, learning, campus software | High-scale B2G and B2C flows, candidate experience |
| TCS MasterCraft | TransformPlus, DataPlus, DevOps tools | Developer tools, GenAI-assisted modernisation |
| TCS Optumera | Retail merchandising AI | Forecasting, pricing, assortment UX |
| Client digital programmes | Banking apps, retail platforms, insurance portals | Product Owner on agile teams |

Locations: Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Gandhinagar and Delhi NCR, with onshore roles in the UK, US, Europe and the Middle East.

## Job Requirements

Qualifications:

- Engineering, MBA or domain degrees (finance, commerce, retail) are common
- Lateral PM roles typically need 4–10 years of experience, often including business analysis or domain consulting
- Domain certifications help: banking (for example, IIBF courses), agile (CSPO, SAFe POPM), cloud fundamentals

Skills:

| Skill | Why it matters at TCS |
| --- | --- |
| Domain knowledge | BaNCS, Optumera and iON serve regulated, complex industries |
| Requirements and backlog management | Most work runs in agile or SAFe programmes |
| Stakeholder management | Clients, delivery leaders and onshore teams all have a say |
| Data and analytics | Adoption, defects and KPIs drive roadmap decisions |
| Communication | Pre-sales demos and client workshops are frequent |
| AI literacy | WisdomNext, ignio and AI features are now part of most roadmaps |

Experience level guide:

- **Campus (0–2 years):** Business analyst or associate product roles; learning the domain is expected
- **Product Owner / PM (4–9 years):** Owns a module or a client product backlog
- **Senior PM (8–13 years):** Owns a product line, influences pre-sales and roadmap
- **Product Head (12+ years):** Owns a product P&L and multiple teams

## Interview Process Breakdown

Lateral process as reported by candidates on AmbitionBox, Glassdoor and Prepfully:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Online Assessment or Screening Call]
    B --> C[Technical and Product Round]
    C --> D[Managerial Round]
    D --> E[HR Round]
    E --> F[Offer]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Phone or iON-based test | 20–60 mins | Background, aptitude or domain basics |
| Technical and product | Video or in person | 45–60 mins | Product lifecycle, go-to-market, agile, domain case |
| Managerial | Video or in person | 30–60 mins | Stakeholder scenarios, client handling, prioritisation |
| HR | Phone or video | 20–30 mins | Compensation, notice period, relocation |

Detailed breakdown:

- Technical and product round:

Candidates report questions on the product lifecycle, writing user stories, defining MVPs and go-to-market plans. Domain teams add specifics: a BaNCS round may ask how a payment flows from UPI to the core ledger, while an iON round may ask how to scale an exam to lakhs of candidates.

- Managerial round:

Expect scenarios such as "A client wants a feature that conflicts with the product roadmap. What do you do?" or "Your release has a critical defect two days before go-live." Interviewers typically look for calm prioritisation and transparent communication.

- Product case:

Some teams ask a short case: design a feature, improve a metric or analyse a drop. Practising with TCS products (for example, improving NQT, measuring ignio success) gives you relevant examples.

- HR round:

Standard discussion of CTC, variable pay, location and joining date. TCS HR policies are structured, so negotiation room depends on level.

Campus process: graduates enter through TCS NQT and are assigned to Ninja, Digital or Prime tracks based on scores and interviews (technical, managerial, HR). MBA hiring at partner campuses includes a resume shortlist, sometimes a group discussion or case, and interviews for business analyst, domain consultant or product roles. Moving into product ownership usually happens after one to three years.

Timeline expectations:

- Lateral: 2–5 weeks
- Campus: results within days of interviews; joining dates can vary

## Product Manager Compensation & Levels at TCS

TCS grades map roughly to product titles:

| Level | Grade (approx.) | Experience | 2026 CTC (INR LPA) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Associate PM / Business Analyst – Product | C2–C3A | 0–4 years | ₹7–13 |
| Product Manager / Product Owner | C3A–C3B | 4–9 years | ₹13–24 |
| Senior Product Manager | C4 | 8–13 years | ₹22–34 |
| Principal PM / Lead PM / Product Head | C5 | 12–17 years | ₹32–48 |
| Director / Head of Product | CXO | 15+ years | ₹50–80 |

Notes:

- Bands are estimates anchored on self-reported AmbitionBox data (PM roughly ₹9–28 LPA for 3–17 years) and vary by unit and city.
- Variable pay is typically 5–15% of CTC, linked to company and unit performance.
- Campus entry: Ninja about ₹3.4–3.6 LPA, Digital about ₹7–7.5 LPA, Prime about ₹9–11.5 LPA (reported figures).
- Onshore assignments in the US, UK or Europe are paid in local currency.

## How to Prepare

Preparation timeline:

1. **Weeks 1–2: Learn the domain.** Pick the unit you are targeting. For BaNCS, learn core banking basics: accounts, ledgers, interest, payments (UPI, NEFT, RTGS, SWIFT). For iON, learn how computer-based exams work. For ignio, read about AIOps and ITSM.
2. **Weeks 2–3: Practise product cases.** Design, improvement, metrics and RCA questions using TCS products.
3. **Week 3: Agile and delivery.** Be ready to write user stories, explain Scrum ceremonies and handle scope changes.
4. **Week 4: Behavioural stories.** Prepare stories on stakeholder conflict, delivery under pressure and influencing without authority.

Practice resources:

- TCS product pages and press releases (BaNCS, ignio, iON, WisdomNext)
- TCS annual reports and earnings call commentary for strategy context
- Gartner and analyst summaries on core banking and AIOps
- NextSprints TCS question bank

> Success tip
> Tie every answer back to client outcomes: fewer outages, faster product launches, lower costs or better exam reliability. TCS sells outcomes to enterprises and governments, and interviewers listen for that framing.

## FAQs

### Does TCS have a formal APM program?

TCS does not run a branded APM programme like some product companies. Graduates usually join through NQT or MBA campus hiring as engineers, business analysts or domain consultants, and move into product owner roles within one to three years. Units such as TCS iON, BaNCS and Digitate also hire associate-level product staff laterally.

### How technical are TCS product interviews?

Moderately technical. You are not expected to code, but you should understand APIs, integration, databases and cloud basics, especially for BaNCS and ignio roles. Candidates report questions on how systems interact and how they would handle defects or performance issues.

### Is domain knowledge mandatory?

For BaNCS and Optumera roles, strong domain knowledge is a major advantage and sometimes required. For iON and client digital programmes, general product skills plus a willingness to learn the domain can be enough at junior levels.

### How long does the TCS PM interview process take?

Lateral candidates typically report 2–5 weeks from first call to offer. Delays usually come from background verification and offer approvals rather than interviews.

### Can I move from a TCS engineering role into product management?

Yes. Internal mobility is common. Engineers often move to business analyst or product owner roles in client programmes, then into product units. Building domain expertise and taking ownership of requirements are the usual stepping stones.

sections.heading: How to Prepare
sections.content:
Company Leadership Principles:

1. Put Customers First: Every product decision should enhance the customer experience.
2. Create Value: Focus on innovations that deliver tangible benefits to customers and the business.
3. Lead with Facts: Use data to drive decisions and measure impact.
4. Embrace Change: Be adaptable and forward-thinking in a rapidly evolving retail landscape.

Tailor Resume: Highlight projects that demonstrate omnichannel thinking and quantifiable impact. Use the STAR method to showcase how you've improved key metrics like conversion rates or customer satisfaction. For example: "Led mobile app redesign, resulting in a 25% increase in in-app purchases and a 15% improvement in user retention."

Practice Product Cases: Focus on retail-specific scenarios that blend digital and physical experiences. Adapt your frameworks to address The Home Depot's unique challenges, such as inventory management across online and in-store channels. NextSprints' interview question database offers a wealth of relevant practice material to hone your skills.

Practice Mock Interviews: While self-practice is valuable, nothing beats real-time feedback from experienced PMs. If you don't have access to mentors in the retail tech space, consider NextSprints' PM coaching for tailored mock sessions that simulate The Home Depot's interview style.

subsections.heading: How does The Home Depot's PM role differ from pure tech companies?
subsections.content: Our PMs need to balance digital innovation with the realities of physical retail. You'll be working on solutions that seamlessly integrate online and in-store experiences, requiring a deep understanding of both technology and traditional retail operations.

subsections.heading: What technologies should I be familiar with?
subsections.content: While you don't need to be an expert coder, familiarity with our tech stack (.NET, React, AWS) is beneficial. More importantly, understand concepts like inventory management systems, point-of-sale technologies, and emerging trends in retail tech like AR/VR for product visualization.

subsections.heading: How important is prior retail experience?
subsections.content: While not mandatory, retail experience is highly valued. However, we also appreciate candidates from other industries who bring fresh perspectives. What's crucial is your ability to quickly grasp retail concepts and apply your PM skills to our unique challenges.

subsections.heading: What's the career progression like for PMs at The Home Depot?
subsections.content: There's significant room for growth. Many of our senior product leaders started as PMs and advanced through the ranks. We also offer opportunities to move between different product areas, from e-commerce to in-store tech to Pro solutions.

subsections.heading: How does The Home Depot support ongoing learning for PMs?
subsections.content: We have a robust professional development program, including regular workshops, conference attendance, and an internal mentorship program. We also encourage PMs to spend time in our stores regularly to stay connected with our core business and customers.

Our PMs need to balance digital innovation with the realities of physical retail. You'll be working on solutions that seamlessly integrate online and in-store experiences, requiring a deep understanding of both technology and traditional retail operations.

While you don't need to be an expert coder, familiarity with our tech stack (.NET, React, AWS) is beneficial. More importantly, understand concepts like inventory management systems, point-of-sale technologies, and emerging trends in retail tech like AR/VR for product visualization.

While not mandatory, retail experience is highly valued. However, we also appreciate candidates from other industries who bring fresh perspectives. What's crucial is your ability to quickly grasp retail concepts and apply your PM skills to our unique challenges.

We have a robust professional development program, including regular workshops, conference attendance, and an internal mentorship program. We also encourage PMs to spend time in our stores regularly to stay connected with our core business and customers.

subsections.content: We have a robust experimentation culture at Uber Freight. We use A/B testing extensively to validate new features and optimizations. PMs are expected to design experiments thoughtfully, considering both the potential business impact and the experience of our users.

subsections.content: Uber Freight offers significant growth opportunities for PMs. As we continue to expand our product offerings and global presence, there are paths to take on larger, more complex products or move into leadership roles. We also encourage lateral moves between different product areas to broaden your expertise. Additionally, the skills you develop here – in areas like marketplace dynamics and logistics optimization – are highly transferable within the broader tech industry.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
UBS is the world's largest wealth manager and, since absorbing Credit Suisse in 2023, by far the biggest bank in Switzerland. Product management at UBS looks different from product management at a consumer tech company. Most roles carry the title **Product Owner** or **Product Manager**, sit inside agile "pods" or "crews" within business divisions, and build platforms for wealthy clients, financial advisors, corporate treasurers, traders and the bank's own operations staff. A smaller set of roles builds consumer-facing apps, such as the UBS & UBS key4 mobile app in Switzerland.

2026 is an unusual moment to join. UBS completed migrating all former Credit Suisse clients onto its systems in March 2026, and the remaining integration work, mainly decommissioning legacy Credit Suisse IT, is expected to be largely finished by the end of the year. At the same time, UBS has rolled out its in-house generative AI assistant Red and Microsoft 365 Copilot across the firm. Product teams are moving from "migrate and stabilise" to "simplify and innovate", which creates opportunities for new product owners in Zurich, the US and the bank's large technology centres in Pune and Hyderabad.

| Hiring Metric | Value (estimate) |
| --- | --- |
| Typical PM / PO titles | Product Owner, Product Manager, Business Product Owner, Digital Product Manager |
| Main hubs | Zurich, Weehawken / New York, Nashville, Pune, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Wroclaw, Krakow, London, Singapore |
| UBS employees in India | 15,000+ across Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad |
| Graduate entry route | Graduate Talent Program (about 24 months) and internships, not a dedicated APM programme |
| Typical time from application to offer | 4–8 weeks (Glassdoor reports average about 39 days for PM roles) |

## Introduction

WEKA's product management culture is at the forefront of innovation in the data storage and management industry. As a leader in AI and machine learning infrastructure, WEKA seeks product managers who can navigate the complexities of high-performance computing while delivering intuitive solutions for enterprise customers.

The role of a product manager at WEKA has never been more critical. With the exponential growth of unstructured data and the increasing adoption of AI workloads, WEKA's products are positioned to revolutionize how organizations handle their most demanding computational challenges. This presents a unique opportunity for product managers to shape the future of data infrastructure.

| Hiring Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| YoY PM team growth | 30% |
| Avg. time-to-hire | 45 days |
| Retention rate | 92% |

> Insider Perspective
> At WEKA, product managers are expected to have a deep understanding of both technical infrastructure and business strategy. The ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear value propositions for C-level executives is paramount.

## PM Role

> WEKA Product Manager
> A WEKA Product Manager leads the development and execution of product strategies that address the evolving needs of enterprise AI and HPC workloads, balancing technical innovation with market demands.

Key responsibilities include:

- Defining product vision and roadmap for WEKA's data platform solutions
- Collaborating with engineering teams to prioritize features and capabilities
- Conducting market research to identify emerging trends in data management
- Developing go-to-market strategies for new product launches
- Analyzing product performance metrics and customer feedback

Team structure:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Chief Product Officer] --> B[VP of Product]
    B --> C[Senior Product Manager]
    C --> D[Product Manager]
    C --> E[Technical Product Manager]
    D --> F[Associate Product Manager]
```

| Aspect | WEKA PM | Google PM | Amazon PM |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Focus | Data infrastructure | Consumer software | E-commerce platforms |
| Technical depth | High | Medium | Medium-High |
| Customer interaction | Enterprise-focused | Limited direct | Varied |
| Product lifecycle | Long-term | Rapid iteration | Mixed |

Real-world example: WEKA's product managers recently spearheaded the development of WEKA 4, which introduced features like snap-to-object to streamline data pipeline efficiency for AI workloads.

## Job Requirements

Education:

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field required
- MBA or advanced degree in a technical field preferred

Experience:

- 5+ years of product management experience in enterprise software or data infrastructure
- Proven track record of successful product launches in the B2B tech space

Technical skills:

- Strong understanding of distributed systems and storage architectures
- Familiarity with AI/ML workflows and data pipeline optimization
- Proficiency in data analysis and SQL
- Experience with agile development methodologies

Soft skills:

- Exceptional communication and presentation abilities
- Strategic thinking and problem-solving aptitude
- Leadership and cross-functional collaboration skills

1. Ability to balance technical depth with business acumen

4. Data-driven decision-making capabilities

> Candidates often underestimate the technical knowledge required for WEKA PM roles. Brush up on your understanding of file systems, object storage, and high-performance computing architectures.

> Expert Advice
> Showcase your ability to think strategically about data infrastructure challenges. Prepare examples of how you've optimized data workflows or improved system performance in previous roles.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content:
Wipro is one of India's largest IT services companies, headquartered in Bengaluru, with roughly US$10.5 billion in annual revenue and about 2.3 lakh employees. Led by CEO Srini Pallia since April 2024, Wipro is repositioning around AI: the Wipro ai360 ecosystem (launched in 2023 with a US$1 billion investment commitment), the Wipro Intelligence suite of AI platforms (including WEGA and WINGS), the Lab45 AI platform, the FullStride Cloud business, and acquisitions such as HARMAN DTS, Mindsprint and Alpha Net in 2025–26.

For students, Wipro is best known for mass campus hiring through Elite NLTH and Turbo. But Wipro also hires product managers, associate product managers and product owners in several places:

- **AI and platform teams:** Lab45, Wipro Intelligence (WEGA, WINGS), legacy automation platforms such as Wipro HOLMES
- **Product businesses:** Topcoder (crowdsourcing marketplace) and Wipro Gallagher Solutions (NetOxygen mortgage loan origination for US lenders)
- **FullStride Cloud and engineering:** Cloud platforms, accelerators and engineering products
- **Client-facing digital programmes:** Product Owner roles on clients' agile teams in banking, retail, healthcare and energy
- **CIO function:** Internal products for Wipro's own employees and operations

| Hiring metric | Estimate |
| --- | --- |
| Product and product owner openings per year (India) | Low hundreds, mostly lateral |
| Main campus routes | Elite NLTH, Turbo, WILP, MBA campus hiring |
| Typical rounds | 3–4 |
| Average time to offer | 2–4 weeks |

> What makes Wipro different
> Candidates report that Wipro product interviews blend product thinking with client and delivery awareness. Interviewers typically want to see that you can design a good product and also explain how it would be delivered, governed and sold to enterprise clients.

sections.heading: PM Role
sections.content:
> Wipro Product Manager
> A Wipro Product Manager or Product Owner defines and delivers AI platforms, software products or client digital products, balancing user needs, client commitments, delivery constraints and Wipro's commercial goals.

Responsibilities:

- Own the roadmap and backlog for a platform, product or client product area
- Translate client and user needs into epics, user stories and acceptance criteria
- Work with engineering, data science, design and delivery teams across India and global locations
- Support pre-sales: demos, solution walkthroughs and RFP responses
- Define and track success metrics such as adoption, productivity gains and client satisfaction
- Ensure responsible AI, security and compliance in AI-driven products

Where PMs sit:

| Area | Product focus | Typical PM work |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lab45 and Wipro Intelligence | AI platforms, agents (WEGA, WINGS) | Agent features, governance, platform adoption |
| FullStride Cloud | Cloud accelerators, FinOps, managed cloud tooling | Productising cloud services |
| Topcoder | Crowdsourcing marketplace | Two-sided marketplace growth and quality |
| Wipro Gallagher Solutions | NetOxygen mortgage LOS | Vertical SaaS for US lenders |
| Client programmes | Banking, retail, healthcare products | Product Owner on agile teams |
| CIO function | Internal tools and platforms | Employee experience products |

Locations: Bengaluru (Sarjapur, Electronic City), Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Noida and Kolkata, plus roles in the US, UK and Europe.

sections.heading: Job Requirements
sections.content:
Qualifications:

- Engineering or MBA degrees are common; domain degrees help for vertical products
- Lateral PM roles generally need 3–10 years of experience
- Agile certifications (CSPO, SAFe POPM) and AI or cloud certifications are valued

Skills:

| Skill | Why it matters at Wipro |
| --- | --- |
| AI and GenAI literacy | Most new products involve AI agents or platforms |
| Enterprise and client empathy | Products are sold to and used by large enterprises |
| Backlog and agile delivery | Most work runs in Scrum or SAFe |
| Data-driven decisions | Productivity and outcome metrics drive deals |
| Communication and stakeholder management | Clients, delivery leaders and global teams |
| Domain knowledge | Banking, insurance, healthcare or retail for vertical roles |

Experience level guide:

- **Campus (0–2 years):** Engineering or business analyst roles; product ownership later
- **Associate PM (1–5 years):** Feature ownership within a platform or product
- **PM / Product Owner (4–9 years):** Own a product area or client product backlog
- **Senior PM (8–14 years):** Own a product line, influence strategy and pre-sales
- **Product Lead / Head (12+ years):** Own portfolios and P&L

sections.heading: Interview Process Breakdown
sections.content:
Lateral process as reported by candidates on Glassdoor, Prepfully, Interview Query and Board Infinity:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Application or Referral] --> B[Online Assessment or Recruiter Screen]
    B --> C[Technical and Product Round 1]
    C --> D[Product or Client Round 2]
    D --> E[Managerial or Culture Fit]
    E --> F[HR]
    F --> G[Offer]
```

| Stage | Format | Duration | Focus areas |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Screening | Phone or online test | 20–60 mins | Background, aptitude, motivation |
| Technical and product round(s) | Video | 45–60 mins each | Product design, agile, metrics, AI awareness |
| Managerial / culture fit | Video or in person | 30–45 mins | Cross-functional leadership, client scenarios |
| HR | Phone or video | 20–30 mins | Compensation, notice, location |

Detailed breakdown:

- Technical and product rounds:

Candidates report product design prompts, agile scenarios and questions on managing cross-functional teams and client interactions. For AI platform roles, expect questions on how you would measure an AI agent's success or govern hundreds of agents.

- Managerial round:

Expect scenarios such as "A client wants a feature that breaks platform standards" or "Your agent's accuracy dropped after a model update." Interviewers typically assess structured thinking and transparent communication.

- Campus product interviews:

One campus candidate reported a single round: an introduction, a product design question and a few HR questions on why they wanted to be a PM at Wipro.

- HR round:

Standard discussion of CTC, variable pay, joining date and location.

Difficulty: Glassdoor reports place the process around 3 out of 5. Timeline: typically 2–4 weeks.

sections.heading: How to Prepare
sections.content:
Preparation timeline:

1. **Week 1: Understand Wipro's AI and platform strategy.** Read about ai360, Wipro Intelligence (WEGA, WINGS), Lab45 and FullStride Cloud.
2. **Week 2: Practise product cases.** Design, improvement, metrics and RCA questions on AI agents, cloud services and marketplaces like Topcoder.
3. **Week 3: Enterprise and delivery thinking.** Learn how services contracts, SLAs and outcome-based pricing work.
4. **Week 4: Behavioural stories.** Prepare examples of stakeholder conflict, delivery under pressure and influencing clients.

Practice resources:

- Wipro press releases, annual reports and earnings call transcripts
- Analyst coverage of agentic services and IT services AI strategies
- NextSprints Wipro question bank

> Success tip
> When you propose a feature, also explain how it would be measured and governed for an enterprise client. Wipro's products are sold on trust and outcomes, so metrics and guardrails make your answers stand out.

subsections.heading: Does Wipro have a formal APM program?
subsections.content: Wipro does not run a widely known branded APM programme. Most graduates join through Elite NLTH, Turbo or MBA campus hiring in engineering, analyst or consulting roles, then move into product ownership. Lab45, Topcoder and platform teams sometimes hire associate PMs laterally.

subsections.heading: How technical are Wipro PM interviews?
subsections.content: Moderately technical. You should understand APIs, cloud basics and how AI models and agents work at a conceptual level. Coding is rarely required, but you may be asked how you would work with engineers on architecture trade-offs.

subsections.heading: What kind of product questions are asked?
subsections.content: Candidates report product design questions, agile and backlog scenarios, metrics questions and cross-functional leadership scenarios. AI-related questions, such as measuring an AI assistant's success, are increasingly common.

subsections.heading: How long does the Wipro PM interview process take?
subsections.content: Typically 2–4 weeks for lateral roles, though approvals and background checks can extend this. Campus processes are usually completed within a day or a few days.

subsections.heading: Can I move from a Wipro engineering role into product management?
subsections.content: Yes. Many product owners start as engineers or business analysts on client programmes. Building domain knowledge, taking ownership of requirements and joining AI platform initiatives are common paths into product roles.
